title: AM Radio: Solid Gold
summary: Hosts announce the 2026 tour dates (January Denver, Seattle, and SketchFest San Francisco; April Madison, Chicago, and Akron) and promote a reprint of the Vinyl episode on Born Losers Records for Record Store Day. The main content traces the history of AM radio: early experiments and the 1920 KDKA Pittsburgh launch, networks, public-good broadcasting and the fairness doctrine, radio soap operas, evangelists and popular shows, the golden age ending in 1962, the rise of Top 40 and DJs, transistor radios and car radios, the yacht rock and Mellow Gold era, and the 2024-2025 fight over AM radio in new cars (AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act, emergency alerts). The episode closes with a listener mail email from Kara.
topics: AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act

segments.title: Tour announcement
segments.summary: Hosts announce 2026 tour dates: January shows in Denver, Seattle and SketchFest in San Francisco, and April shows in Madison, Chicago and Akron, with presale code details.

segments.title: Vinyl episode reprint promotion
segments.summary: Promotion for the reprinted Vinyl episode record on Born Losers Records, available for Record Store Day on November 28 at syskvinyl.com.

segments.title: Early AM radio and its spread
segments.summary: Early AM broadcasting from the 1900s, the 1920 KDKA Pittsburgh launch, AT&T's 1922 network, spread to the BBC, Australia and Canada, household adoption, and the FM versus AM frequency bands.

segments.title: Golden age of radio programming
segments.summary: Early radio programming including sports broadcasts, presidential addresses, FDR's fireside chats, soap operas sponsored by cleaning companies, Guiding Light, religious evangelists, Edgar Bergen and Charlie McCarthy, and the 1962 cancellations of Johnny Dollar and Suspense as the end of the golden age.

segments.title: Public good and the fairness doctrine
segments.summary: Government early role in radio for public information, USDA radio service and home economics programs, and the fairness doctrine requiring equal time on political matters and preventing commercial interests from overriding public service.

segments.title: FM growth, talk radio and clear channels
segments.summary: The fairness doctrine's end as FM grew, the rise of talk radio in the 1980s, AM nighttime signal limits and sign-offs, skywave propagation via the ionosphere, and clear channel stations that broadcast 24 hours and serve as a national alert system.

segments.title: Top 40, DJs and the rise of music on AM
segments.summary: Top 40 format developed on AM by Todd Storz in Nebraska in the early 1950s, the rise of DJ personalities such as Wolfman Jack and the Big Bopper, and the move of older listeners to TV leaving AM to young listeners, plus transistor and car radios.

segments.title: Yacht rock and Mellow Gold
segments.summary: AM's 1970s and early 1980s yacht rock and Mellow Gold era, sad-sack songs, hidden meanings in lyrics, the yacht rock documentary and the term's origin, and discussion of songs by Christopher Cross and Rupert Holmes.

segments.title: AM radio in electric vehicles and the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act
segments.summary: Automakers including Tesla dropping AM radio in EVs due to electrical interference, the government's emergency alert rationale, crystal radios, car makers' positions, and the AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act failing in 2024 and being reintroduced in 2025.
topics: AM Radio for Every Vehicle Act

segments.title: Listener mail from Kara
segments.summary: Kara writes about listening since 2008 during high school illness, seeing the show live in Boston, and catching up on episodes; hosts thank her and invite listener mail.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Closing credits and iHeartRadio production note.
